prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Lange deutsche Komposita (language de).
Grid: 3 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Begriff" · longest unbreakable word 546px · one-line width 546px
  col 2: header "Kurzform" · longest unbreakable word 83px · one-line width 101px
  col 3: header "Erklärung" · longest unbreakable word 186px · one-line width 1091px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 720px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 719px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 720px. You MAY choose a total wider than 719px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 720px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"A German glossary/reference table for very long compound terms, pairing each term with its abbreviation and a plain-language explanation.","reading":"Readers locate a row by scanning the full compound term or its short form, then read the explanation. Comparison happens mainly within a row, not across numeric columns.","groups":["Columns 1–2 form the identifier pair: the full compound and its abbreviation name the same entity and should stay adjacent and visually linked.","Column 3 is supporting prose, subordinate to the identifier pair and read after it."],"keep_intact":["Abbreviations in column 2, especially hyphenated forms such as Kfz-Haftpflicht","The 186px unbreakable word in column 3 if possible","Compound terms in column 1 where width allows; split only when necessary"],"may_wrap":["Explanation prose at word spaces","Long compound terms in column 1 when the chosen width cannot hold them","Column headers if needed"]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[360,122,237],"idea":"Identifier-first fit: give the full term and abbreviation enough room to stay scannable while the explanation wraps in a narrow but readable column."},{"name":"B","widths":[220,122,377],"idea":"Explanation-first fit: prioritize readable explanation text and accept multi-line compound terms while keeping the abbreviation rail intact."},{"name":"C","widths":[567,122,1112],"idea":"No-split horizontal layout: preserve every cell on one line and let the reader scroll horizontally rather than split any word."}]}
